4. Constructional

4.1 The face of the dial shall be suitably marked with their application, that is, `AIR' or `OIL' symbolically, as the case may be, and the unit of measurement in kPa. The manufacturer's monogram shall also be marked. These markings shall be of such a size and shall be so located as to not to be obscured at any pointer position. 4.2 The dial scale shall increase from low to high readings in a clockwise direction. A simple number style shall be used. The letters and markings shall be large enough for easy identification and reading. Number shall be oriented to read in a horizontal `arcuate' arrangement. 4.3 The pointer shall be of simple, symmetrical 4.4 The mounting becoming loose. 4.5 All terminals, 5. and

keys and fasteners shall be robust and shall withstand

a torque force of 20 kgf.

5.1.2 Accuracy test - All pressure gauges shall be tested for accuracy over the entire error in pressure indication on any point shall not exceed &2 percent of the maximum The response time shall not be more than one second. 5.2 Type Tests The following shall constitute type tests:

5.3 Endurance Test-The gauge shall be subjected to cyclic pressure fluctuations for 1 00 000 cycles at a frequency of 2515 cycles per minute in such a way that the pointer deflects approximately between 0 and 100 percent of the full scale reading. After completion of the above cycles, the accuracy of the reading shall be within &3 percent of the full scale deflection. 5.4 Dry Heat Test ~ The gauges shall be subjected to a test temperature cf 85�C fcr a period cf 4 h with a recovery period of 2 h. When subjected to performance test after the conditioning, the accuracy of the reading shall be within :t3 percent of the full scale deflection. 2

5.7 Water Spray Test -The test shall be conducted for a period of 2 hours. The gauge, before subjecting to the test, shall be mounted in a box facing the dial upwards so as to expose only the external parts. The gauge shall then be tested for performance and the accuracy of the reading should be within h3 percent of the full scale value. There shall not be any ingress of water in the gauge. 5.8 Vibration Test - Shall be increased to two hours. Note comply with 4.1 of IS : 10250-1982. The test duration in each axis shall

5.9 Drop Test - The gauge after mounting on a simulating support shall be allowed from a height of 500 mm on a level concrete surface. This shall be repeated 50 times. the gauge shall not show any sign of damage. The accuracy of the readings shall percent of the full scale value.

5.10 Dust Test - Shall comply with IS : 9000 (Part 12)-1981 `Dust test'. At the end of the test, the exterior surface is cleaned and subjected to the performance test. The accuracy of the readings shall be within 1l13 percent of the full scale deflection, and also there shall not be any ingress of dust inside the gauge. 5.11 Corrosion Resistance Test - This test is conducted on the sample in a suitable chamber by spraying with a 5 percent solution of sodium chloride in water at 27f-2�C. The test duration shall be 50 hours consisting of two cycles each of 24 hours spray and one hour drain periods. After removal from the chamber, the sample shall not show any evidence of corrosion. When tested for accuracy, the readings shall be within *3 percent of the full scale deflection. 5.12 Bump Test - Shall for accuracy, the readings 5.13 impact the readings comply with IS : 9000 (Part 7/Set 1 to 5)-1979 `Impact shall be within f3 percent of the full scale deflection. 7. Packing - A suitable protective cap shall be used on the inlet and threaded portions of the gauges. Each gauge shall be packed in carton suitably cushioned to prevent any movement. 8. Sampling - Unless otherwise agreed upon, the sampling scheme for testing purposes shall be in accordance with IS : 2500 (Part l)-1973 `Sampling inspection tables: Part 1 Inspection by attributes and by count of defects (first revision 1'.

EXPLANATORY

NOTE

This standard relates to pressure gauges of direct reading type suitable for automotives with common working fluids, such as oil and air. It is applicable only to individual assemblies and not to a cluster of gauges. While preparing this standard for automotive use, assistance has been derived from the following: IS : 3624-l IS : 10250-l IS : 9000 979 982 Pressure and vacuum gauges ( first revision Severities for environmental )

tests for automotive electrical equipment testing procedures for electronic

Series of standards on `Basic environmental and electrical items'. 4
